source.author: Al Brooks
source.chapter_title: Example of How to Trade a Trend

conventions: stop entries mechanized as signal-bar-close then next-bar-open; every tunable constant is a parameter; long side only in pseudocode; sides field states mirrored/same

candidates.name: MovingAverageTouch
candidates.quote: Buying a high 2 pullback to the moving average in a bull trend.
candidates.description: Primitive: the current bar's range includes (touches or crosses) the moving average.
candidates.pseudocode: low[0] <= ema[0] && high[0] >= ema[0]
candidates.book_order_type: n/a (bar classification)

complexity.reason: needs an EMA value per bar

notes: Shared primitive for this chapter's several 'pullback to the moving average' setups.

candidates.name: SecondPullbackSignal
candidates.quote: Buying a high 2 pullback to the moving average in a bull trend.
candidates.description: Primitive: a high 2 (H2) buy setup -- the second distinct pullback leg against a bull trend, triggered by a break of the first pullback's high after the market made a lower high than the first pullback's low point of return. Needs leg/pivot detection to count pullbacks.
candidates.pseudocode: // needs swing-pivot/leg counting (as in 20_two_legs.txt): identify pullback leg 1's low and recovery high, then pullback leg 2, and signal on leg 2's high being taken out
candidates.book_order_type: stop entry one tick above the signal bar (leg 2's high), mechanized as signal-bar-close then next-bar-open

complexity.reason: needs swing-pivot/leg counting, same dependency as the two-legged-pullback primitives in 20_two_legs.txt

notes: Shared primitive for every 'high 2' / 'low 2' setup named in this chapter; expect this to merge with T20-02/T20-04 in dedup.

candidates.name: WedgeFlagPattern
candidates.quote: Buying a wedge bull flag pullback in a bull trend.
candidates.description: Primitive: a three-push wedge-shaped flag against the trend, where each push makes a new (or equal) extreme but with less momentum, converging toward a point -- entry on the break of the wedge's most recent extreme.
candidates.pseudocode: // needs three-pivot detection (push1, push2, push3) with a convergence/momentum-decline test between pushes
candidates.book_order_type: stop entry one tick beyond the wedge's most recent extreme, mechanized as signal-bar-close then next-bar-open

complexity.reason: needs swing-pivot detection over a variable-length three-push window plus a convergence test

candidates.name: BreakoutPullbackEntry
candidates.quote: Buying a breakout pullback after a breakout from a bull flag in a bull trend.
candidates.description: Primitive: after price breaks out above a bull flag's high, a shallow pullback that does not erase the breakout, followed by a resumption above the pullback bar's high, is a breakout-pullback buy.
candidates.pseudocode: // needs flag/range detection, a breakout event (close[k] > flagHigh), then a pullback bar whose low stays above flagHigh, then entry above that pullback bar's high
candidates.book_order_type: stop entry one tick above the pullback bar's high, mechanized as signal-bar-close then next-bar-open

complexity.reason: needs flag/range identification plus a persisted breakout level and a pullback test against it

notes: Shared primitive; reused for several bullet points and for the 'anticipating a breakout pullback' setup below (T18-18).

candidates.name: BullSpikeClassification
candidates.quote: Buying a bull spike in a strong bull breakout at the market, at the close of every bull trend bar in the spike.
candidates.description: Primitive: an active bull spike -- a short run of consecutive bull trend bars with high body fraction and little overlap, following a breakout.
candidates.pseudocode: countIf(i, 0, spikeWindow - 1, close[i] > open[i] && (close[i]-open[i]) >= bodyFraction*(high[i]-low[i])) >= spikeWindow * minFraction
candidates.book_order_type: n/a (state classification)

complexity.reason: window loop counting a per-bar trend-bar classification

notes: Brooks gives no numeric definition of a 'spike'; parameters are a reading of the concept.

candidates.name: BuyClimaxBar
candidates.quote: Buying a high 1 pullback in a strong bull spike in a bull trend, but not after a buy climax.
candidates.description: Primitive: an exceptionally large, extended bull trend bar occurring late in a mature bull move -- a buy climax that warrants a larger correction rather than an immediate with-trend entry.
candidates.pseudocode: // needs a design decision on what qualifies as a 'climax' bar (extreme range relative to recent bars + an already-extended prior move)
candidates.book_order_type: n/a (state classification used to suppress other entries)

complexity.reason: Brooks does not give a numeric test for 'climax'; same open question as T19-17 (NoClimaxBar)

candidates.name: HighOnePullbackInSpikeNotAfterClimax
candidates.quote: Buying a high 1 pullback in a strong bull spike in a bull trend, but not after a buy climax.
candidates.description: Buy the first pullback (H1) within an active bull spike (T18-05), unless a buy climax (T18-06) has just occurred.
candidates.pseudocode: BullSpikeActive() && !BuyClimaxBar() && low[0] < low[1] && close[0] > open[0]
candidates.book_order_type: stop entry one tick above the pullback bar's high, mechanized as signal-bar-close then next-bar-open

complexity.reason: inherits the spike-classification and research-grade climax dependencies

candidates.name: BuyStopAboveSwingHighVeryStrongTrend
candidates.quote: When a bull trend is very strong, buying on a stop above a prior swing high.
candidates.description: In a very strong bull trend, place a buy stop above the most recent swing high rather than waiting for a pullback.
candidates.pseudocode: VeryStrongBullTrend() && close[0] <= mostRecentSwingHigh
candidates.book_order_type: stop entry one tick above the prior swing high

complexity.reason: the stop-placement test itself is simple, but 'very strong trend' is a research-grade classification (as in T19-24)

candidates.name: BuySpikeAtCloseOfEachTrendBar
candidates.quote: Buying a bull spike in a strong bull breakout at the market, at the close of every bull trend bar in the spike.
candidates.description: While an active bull spike (T18-05) is in progress, buy at the close of every bull trend bar within it.
candidates.pseudocode: BullSpikeActive() && close[0] > open[0] && (close[0]-open[0]) >= bodyFraction*(high[0]-low[0])
candidates.book_order_type: market order at the close of the bar; mechanized as the close condition true on bar 0, filled at next bar's open

complexity.reason: combines a per-bar trend-bar test with the spike-state dependency

candidates.name: BuySpikeLimitBelowPriorBarLow
candidates.quote: ...or on a limit order at or below the low of the prior bar (entering in spikes requires a wider stop and the spike happens quickly, so this combination is difficult for many traders).
candidates.description: While an active bull spike is in progress, place a limit buy at or below the low of the prior bar.
candidates.pseudocode: BullSpikeActive() && low[0] <= low[1]
candidates.book_order_type: limit order at or below the prior bar's low, filled intrabar

complexity.reason: a simple price test gated by the spike-state dependency

candidates.name: BuyCloseFirstBearBarInBullSpike
candidates.quote: Buying the close of the first bear bar in a bull spike.
candidates.description: Buy at the close of the first bar that closes down (a bear bar) after an active bull spike has been running -- traders expect the countertrend bar to fail immediately.
candidates.pseudocode: BullSpikeActive(1) && close[1] > open[1] && close[0] < open[0]
candidates.book_order_type: market order at the close of the bear bar; mechanized as the condition true on bar 0, filled at next bar's open

complexity.reason: needs the spike-state dependency plus a 'first' qualifier (prior bar still in the spike, current bar breaks it)

candidates.name: BuyAtBullTrendLineOrPriorSwingLow
candidates.quote: In a bull trend, buying at a bull trend line or at a prior swing low (a potential double bottom bull flag).
candidates.description: In a bull trend, buy on a limit order at the bull trend line, or at a prior swing low forming a potential double bottom.
candidates.pseudocode: // needs trend-line projection from pivots (for the trend-line touch) OR low[0] near a prior recorded swing low (for the double-bottom case)
candidates.book_order_type: limit order at the trend line or at/near the prior swing low

complexity.reason: needs swing-pivot detection and, for the trend-line branch, trend-line projection

candidates.name: BuyWeakSignalBarLimitNewBullTrend
candidates.quote: Buying at or below a low 1 or 2 weak signal bar on a limit order in a possible new bull trend after a strong reversal up or at the bottom of a trading range.
candidates.description: After a strong reversal up, or at the bottom of a trading range, buy at or below a weak (small-bodied, poor-looking) low 1 or low 2 signal bar on a limit order, anticipating the weak countertrend signal fails.
candidates.pseudocode: // needs: (a) the H1/H2-style pullback-count primitive (T18-02) applied to a 'low 1/2' countertrend signal that is against the *new*, not-yet-confirmed trend, and (b) a 'weak bar' quality test (small body fraction)
candidates.book_order_type: limit order at or below the weak signal bar's low

complexity.reason: combines the leg-counting dependency of T18-02 with a bar-quality test and a 'possible new trend / bottom of trading range' context that itself needs a trading-range definition

candidates.name: BuyPriorBarLimitQuietFlagAtMA
candidates.quote: Buying at or below the prior bar on a limit order in a quiet bull flag at the moving average.
candidates.description: In a quiet (small-range, low-volatility) bull flag sitting at the moving average (T18-01), place a limit buy at or below the prior bar's low.
candidates.pseudocode: MovingAverageTouch() && (high[0]-low[0]) <= quietRangeMultiple*average(high[0..lookback-1]-low[0..lookback-1]) && low[0] <= low[1]
candidates.book_order_type: limit order at or below the prior bar's low

complexity.reason: combines the EMA-touch primitive with a simple window-average 'quiet' range test

candidates.name: BuyBelowBullBarBreakoutAboveFlag
candidates.quote: Buying below a bull bar that breaks above a bull flag, anticipating a breakout pullback.
candidates.description: As soon as a bull bar closes above a bull flag's high (the breakout bar itself), place a limit buy below that breakout bar, anticipating the breakout-pullback entry of T18-04 will follow.
candidates.pseudocode: close[0] > open[0] && close[0] > flagHigh && close[1] <= flagHigh
candidates.book_order_type: limit order below the breakout bar's low or midpoint

complexity.reason: shares the flag/breakout-level dependency of T18-04

candidates.name: BuyBreakoutTestToAddForSwing
candidates.quote: When trying for a swing in a bull trend, buy or buy more on a breakout test, which is an attempt to run breakeven stops from an earlier long entry.
candidates.description: While holding (or after) an earlier with-trend long, add to the position when price retests (a 'breakout test' of) the level where earlier longs placed breakeven stops, expecting that stop-running move to fail and the trend to resume.
candidates.pseudocode: ctx.MarketPosition() > 0 && low[0] <= ctx.EntryPrice() && close[0] >= ctx.EntryPrice()
candidates.book_order_type: buy more at the market or on a limit order at the retest level

complexity.reason: reads position state (EntryPrice) but the retest test itself is a plain price comparison

notes: 'Buy more' is an add-to-position action; the engine's per-bar boolean Entry role can express the trigger but not the position-sizing math.

candidates.name: BuyFixedTicksDownFromHigh
candidates.quote: Buying at a fixed number of ticks down from the high in a bull trend. For example, buying a two-, three-, or four-point pullback in a bull trend in the Emini.
candidates.description: Place a limit buy a fixed distance below the most recent swing/trend high.
candidates.pseudocode: low[0] <= highest(high, lookback) - pullbackPoints
candidates.book_order_type: limit order at a fixed distance below the recent high

complexity.reason: a window-highest lookup compared against a fixed offset

notes: Brooks also describes calibrating pullbackPoints to the day's own biggest pullback so far -- an adaptive variant not captured here for simplicity.

candidates.name: BuyAtMovingAverageAfterGapBarStreakLimit
candidates.quote: In a bull trend that has not pulled back to the moving average in 20 or more bars, buy at the moving average on a limit order, and scale in lower.
candidates.description: Once the trend has gone at least N consecutive bars without the moving average touch of T18-01, place a limit buy one tick above the moving average (the '20 gap bar' buy setup).
candidates.pseudocode: countConsecutive(i => low[i] > ema[i], gapBarCount) == gapBarCount && low[0] <= ema[0] + oneTick
candidates.book_order_type: limit order one tick above the moving average

complexity.reason: a persisted streak counter on top of the EMA primitive

notes: Same concept as T19-13 (MovingAverageGapBarStreak); expect these to merge in dedup.

candidates.name: BuyCloseFirstBearTrendBarBelowMaInStrongTrend
candidates.quote: In a strong bull trend, buy on the close of the first bear trend bar that has a close below the moving average.
candidates.description: In a strong bull trend, buy at the close of the first bear trend bar whose close falls below the moving average (the prior bar's close having been at/above it).
candidates.pseudocode: close[1] >= ema[1] && close[0] < open[0] && (open[0]-close[0]) >= bodyFraction*(high[0]-low[0]) && close[0] < ema[0]
candidates.book_order_type: market order at the close of the bar; mechanized as the condition true on bar 0, filled at next bar's open

complexity.reason: a two-bar EMA-relative test plus a trend-bar classification; the 'strong trend' qualifier is left as an external gate

candidates.name: BuyFailedBreakoutBelowSwingLowInPullback
candidates.quote: In a strong bull trend, a pullback is a small bear trend. The bulls will expect that a breakout below a prior swing low in this small bear trend will fail, and they will buy there with a limit order.
candidates.description: Within a pullback (a small countertrend move) inside a strong bull trend, place a limit buy at/below the prior swing low reached during that pullback, anticipating any further breakout below it will fail.
candidates.pseudocode: // needs: (a) identification of the current pullback's own most recent internal swing low, (b) a limit order placed at/below it
candidates.book_order_type: limit order at or below the pullback's internal swing low

complexity.reason: needs swing-pivot detection scoped to the current pullback, plus the research-grade 'strong trend' context

candidates.name: AlwaysInLongBlocksShorts
candidates.quote: A trader can always be long, short, or flat. At any moment during a trend, only two of those choices are compatible with being a successful trader. If the market is in a bull trend, successful traders are only long or flat.
candidates.description: While the market is classified 'always-in long' (a bull trend is in effect), block new short entries and prefer flat over short.
candidates.pseudocode: // needs a design decision on how 'always-in direction' is classified from bars (the concept itself is central to the trilogy but never reduced to a formula here)
candidates.book_order_type: n/a (a global gate on entries, not itself an order)

complexity.reason: 'always-in direction' is the canonical example of a concept that needs a design decision before it can be coded (per MINING.md)

candidates.name: TrailStopBelowRecentHigherLowOnNewHigh
candidates.quote: After every new high, he tightened his stop to below the most recent higher low, since as long as the trend kept making higher highs and lows, it was still strong.
candidates.description: Each time price makes a new swing high while long, move the protective stop to one tick below the most recently confirmed swing low.
candidates.pseudocode: high[0] > highest(high[1..swingLookback], swingLookback) => trailStopPrice = mostRecentSwingLow - oneTick
candidates.book_order_type: stop order trailed to just below the most recent swing low

complexity.reason: needs swing-low pivot detection plus a new-high trigger to update the stop

notes: Distinct from the catalog's profit-based TrailingStop/AtrTrailingStop: the trail level here is a price pivot (swing low), not a dollar amount below peak profit.

candidates.name: PartialProfitAboveMostRecentHigh
candidates.quote: if their profit is large enough, they should consider taking partial profits as the market goes above the most recent high.
candidates.description: Once open profit is sufficiently large, take a partial profit as price trades above the most recent swing high.
candidates.pseudocode: ctx.OpenPositionProfit() >= profitThreshold && high[0] > mostRecentSwingHigh
candidates.book_order_type: limit/market order to scale out part of the position above the recent high

complexity.reason: needs a swing-high pivot plus an open-profit threshold; the engine's Exit role fires a full exit, so 'partial' is a modeling limitation, not a coding difficulty

notes: Partial exits are not directly representable if the engine's Exit closes the whole position; recorded as a full-exit approximation.

candidates.name: MoveStopToBreakevenAfterRetestAndNewHigh
candidates.quote: Many traders moved their stops to breakeven once there was a pullback that tested their entry price and then the market reached a new high. They did not want the market to come back down to their entry price a second time.
candidates.description: Once price has pulled back to retest the original entry price and then gone on to make a new high, move the protective stop to breakeven.
candidates.pseudocode: hasRetestedEntryPrice && high[0] > highest(high[1..lookback], lookback) => stopPrice = ctx.EntryPrice()
candidates.book_order_type: stop order moved to the entry price

complexity.reason: needs a persisted flag for 'has retested entry price since entry' plus a new-high test

candidates.name: StopBeyondFractionOfAverageDailyRange
candidates.quote: Some traders will consider that the trend is still in effect unless the market falls more than between 50 to 75 percent of the average daily range.
candidates.description: Treat the trend (and the open long) as still intact, and hold the position, until the pullback from the recent high exceeds a fraction of the average daily range; exit once it does.
candidates.pseudocode: (mostRecentSwingHigh - low[0]) > adrFraction * averageDailyRange(lookbackDays)
candidates.book_order_type: stop order placed/trailed at that distance below the recent high

complexity.reason: needs a swing-high pivot plus a daily-range average computed across sessions

notes: Distinct from AtrTrailingStop: anchored to price (a swing high) with a fraction of the average DAILY (session) range, not a dollar amount below peak profit using a bar-level ATR.

candidates.name: ProfitTargetAtInitialRiskMultiple
candidates.quote: A trader should exit a trade only when the chance of success ... times the potential reward is significantly greater than the chance of failure ... times the risk. ... they should not take any profit until the trade has gone at least two points ... twice their initial risk.
candidates.description: Do not take any profit until open profit reaches at least N times the position's own initial risk (entry price minus the initial protective stop price); take a (partial) profit once it does.
candidates.pseudocode: ctx.OpenPositionProfit() >= riskMultiple * initialRiskAtEntry
candidates.book_order_type: limit order to take profit at N times the initial risk

complexity.reason: needs the trade's own initial risk (entry minus initial stop) persisted from the moment of entry

notes: Distinct from AtrProfitTarget/TakeProfitWithRatioStop: the multiple is applied to THIS trade's own initial stop distance, not an ATR reading or a fixed dollar figure.

candidates.name: TieredRiskMultipleScaleOut
candidates.quote: they might have taken a quarter off after a $1.00 profit and another quarter off at $2.00, and maybe a third quarter at $3.00, and held onto the final quarter until either a strong sell signal formed or until the end of the day.
candidates.description: Scale out in quarters as open profit reaches successive multiples (1x, 2x, 3x) of the initial risk, holding the final quarter until a strong reversal signal or the session close.
candidates.pseudocode: ctx.OpenPositionProfit() >= tier1Multiple * initialRiskAtEntry // scale out 1st quarter, then repeat at tier2Multiple, tier3Multiple; final quarter exits on TimeOfDayExit or a reversal signal
candidates.book_order_type: successive limit orders to scale out a quarter of the position at each tier

complexity.reason: multiple profit tiers each needing the same persisted initial-risk state as T18-26, plus partial-exit modeling limitations and a session-close fallback

notes: Structurally resembles TieredProfitProtector (tiered floors with rising treatment) but tiers are risk-multiples from entry, not absolute profit floors with a retracement ratio.

candidates.name: EnterAtMarketOnceInTrend
candidates.quote: When the market is in a trend, traders should look for any reason to enter. The simple existence of a trend is reason enough to enter at least a small position at the market.
candidates.description: As soon as the market is classified as being in a trend (any trend, not necessarily a strong one), enter at the market rather than waiting for a specific setup.
candidates.pseudocode: // needs a design decision on how 'is in a trend' is classified from bars; once true, enter at the market unconditionally
candidates.book_order_type: market order

complexity.reason: depends entirely on an undefined 'is the market in a trend' classification -- the same open design question as always-in direction (T18-21) and the strong-trend composite (T19-24)

notes: Weaker version of T19-24 (StrongTrendComposite): any trend qualifies here, not just a strong one.

rejected.quote: Scaling into the direction of the trend as the market moves against you. If you scale in, plan out in advance what size each order has to be to keep your total risk the same as with a typical trade.
rejected.reason: position sizing / scaling math is not represented in the engine's per-bar boolean entry/exit rule model

rejected.quote: trade only when the chance of success times the potential reward is significantly greater than the chance of failure times the risk.
rejected.reason: requires a subjective, un-computable probability-of-success estimate; no bar-level data supplies it

rejected.quote: Only the most experienced traders should consider scalping, because the risk is sometimes greater than the potential reward. This means that they have to win about 70 percent of the time.
rejected.reason: pure discretion about trader skill/experience level, no bar-level test

rejected.quote: These old highs are often the highs of higher time frame bars, like on the 15 or 60 minute charts, so the entry is usually a breakout above the high of a prior bull trend bar on these higher time frame charts.
rejected.reason: requires a different, higher-timeframe bar series that the engine does not have alongside the single configured bar series

rejected.quote: Experienced traders have a good sense of when the market is transitioning from a trend into a trading range, and many will exit the remainder of their positions when they believe that it is about to happen.
rejected.reason: pure discretion ('a good sense'), no bar-level test given

rejected.quote: Once the trend enters its channel phase, it always looks like it is reversing... Swing traders who are comfortable taking low probability buy setups near the top of weak bull channels love this kind of price action.
rejected.reason: narrative trader-psychology commentary, no bar-level test

chapter_summary: The chapter opens with an explicit checklist of roughly 20 concrete with-trend entry techniques for trading an established trend (H2/moving-average pullbacks, wedge and breakout-pullback flags, H1 spike pullbacks excluding buy climaxes, buying strength directly in a spike, trend-line/double-bottom entries, fixed-tick pullback entries, the 20-gap-bar moving-average buy, and the always-in long/flat constraint), all mined here as Entry candidates -- most graded hard because they depend on the same swing-pivot/leg-counting and trend-line-projection primitives that recur across the trilogy (shared here as T18-01 through T18-06). The remainder of the chapter is two long worked GS chart examples (Figures 18.1-18.2) that narrate a full trend day almost bar by bar, reusing these same setups plus concepts defined in other chapters (double bottoms, triangles, third pushes, always-in); it is not re-mined bar-by-bar. It also contains real, previously-uncaptured trade-management rules mined as Exit candidates: trailing the stop below each new higher swing low, moving the stop to breakeven after a retest-then-new-high, bounding the acceptable pullback to a fraction of the average daily range, and taking (partial) profits only once open profit reaches a multiple of the trade's own initial risk, including a tiered quarter-by-quarter scale-out. A large fraction of the chapter's remaining text is position-sizing arithmetic and trader psychology/discretion, rejected as not bar-decidable.
